parts.problem_md: Identify which characteristic describes a public sector organisation.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **The correct answer is B** (Exists to provide a service to the community)

parts.problem_md: State **one **difference between the objectives of private sector organisations and public sector organisations.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award marks as indicated. **
> 
> The objective of private sector organisations is to generate a profit **(1)** whereas the objective of public sector organisations is to provide a service to the general public **(1)**.
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses.**

parts.problem_md: Identify **three **stakeholders that may have an interest in the financial statements of a private sector organisation.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award marks as indicated (maximum 3 marks). **
> 
> - Suppliers / Trade payables
> - Customers / Trade receivables
> - Providers of finance / Banks
> - Government
> - Employees
> - Owners
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses.**

parts.problem_md:
State **one **advantage and **one **disadvantage of forming a partnership.

Advantage .........................................

Disadvantage .....................................
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award mark as indicated.**
> 
> **Advantages Max (1) **
> 
> Additional capital **(1) **
> More expertise** (1) **
> Shared work load** (1) **
> 
> **Disadvantages Max (1)**
> 
> Shared profits **(1) **
> Disputes **(1) **
> Lack of control **(1) **
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses**

parts.problem_md: State **two **advantages of operating a business as a sole trader.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award 1 mark for each advantage up to maximum of 2 marks.**
> 
> Easy to set up **(1)**.
> 
> Keeps all profit **(1)**.
> 
> Retains full control **(1)**.
> 
> Quick decision making **(1)**.

>

>

>

>

>

parts.problem_md: Evaluate whether a sole trader should form a partnership.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award up to 2 marks for identification, 2 marks for development and 1 mark for conclusion. **
> 
> **Sample answers **
> 
> A sole trader may have limited finance/capital/resources to expand the business **(1)**, but a new partner brings in additional finance/capital/resources available to expand the business  **(1)**.
> 
> A sole trader may find it hard to cope with the demands of the increased business  **(1)**, but a new partner will bring in additional skills/knowledge/ideas/ and share workload  **(1)**.
> 
> If a sole trader forms a partnership, he will lose control as all the decision are to be made collectively (1), whereas at present he makes all the decisions  **(1)**.
> 
> If a sole trader forms a partnership, he must share the profits with the other partner  **(1)**, whereas at present he takes all the profits  **(1)**.
> 
> Any supported decision  **(1)**.
